text.title: Uncontrolled runtime upgrades
text.problem: Image rebuilds can select a different Python version without a source change.
text.consequence: The application can run on a Python version that CI does not check.
text.fix: Restore the explicit Python and distribution version.

text.title: Search bypasses the shared get_db helper
text.problem: search_items opens its own connection with a hardcoded path. It does not call the shared get_db helper.
text.consequence: A future change to DATABASE in server.py will not reach the search route. The two routes could then read different databases.
text.fix: Move get_db into a shared module and call it from search_items. Use it as a context manager like the other routes do.

text.title: Search bypasses the shared get_db helper
text.problem: search_items opens its own connection to a hardcoded items.db path instead of calling get_db. An exception in execute skips conn.close.
text.consequence: A change to DATABASE in server.py leaves search reading a different database. Failed queries leave the connection open until garbage collection.
text.fix: Move get_db to a shared module and call it from search_items. Close the connection with contextlib.closing or a try and finally block.

text.title: Unbounded search results
text.problem: Search loads and serializes every matching row without pagination.
text.consequence: Requests matching many rows can exhaust worker memory or delay other users' requests.
text.fix: Apply a bounded SQL LIMIT and expose pagination before fetching matching rows.

text.title: Unbounded index lock acquisition
text.problem: The migration sets no lock timeout before requesting a SHARE lock on items.
text.consequence: An existing writer can stall the migration and queue later writers behind its lock request.
text.fix: Set a short lock_timeout before creating the index.

truth.text: CREATE INDEX without CONCURRENTLY holds a lock that blocks every insert and update on items until the index is built, so the shop stops taking writes for as long as the build takes on a large table. The fix is CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, outside a transaction.

text.title: No statement timeout for index build
text.problem: The migration does not set statement_timeout before the index build.
text.consequence: A slow index build can run with no limit and hold its lock the whole time.
text.fix: Set statement_timeout before the CREATE INDEX statement, sized to the expected build time.

text.fix: Add IF NOT EXISTS to the CREATE INDEX statement.

text.title: API container runs privileged with privilege escalation allowed
text.problem: The change sets privileged to true and allowPrivilegeEscalation to true on the api container. Privileged mode grants every capability and overrides the drop ALL list at line 46.
text.consequence: An attacker who compromises the API process can gain root on the node and escape the container. The readiness and liveness probes use httpGet, so the health check gains nothing from this access.
text.fix: Restore allowPrivilegeEscalation to false and remove the privileged setting. If the app truly needs raw sockets, add only the NET_RAW capability.

@@ -38,7 +38,9 @@ spec:

             - containerPort: 5000
           securityContext:
-            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
+            # The health check pings the database host with raw sockets.
+            privileged: true
+            allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
             readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
             capabilities:
               drop: ["ALL"]

truth.text: privileged: true gives the API container every capability and the node's devices, so a flaw in the app becomes root on the node; allowPrivilegeEscalation: true lets its processes gain more privileges than they started with. A raw-socket health check needs only the NET_RAW capability, so the fix is to drop privileged, keep allowPrivilegeEscalation false and add NET_RAW alone.

text.title: Unchecked row cleanup error
text.problem: Search discards the error returned by rows.Close.
text.consequence: Search provides no diagnostic if deferred row cleanup fails.
text.fix: Search should explicitly handle or document the discarded cleanup error.

text.title: Missing rows.Err check after the row loop
text.problem: Search never calls rows.Err after rows.Next returns false. Search then encodes the users read so far.
text.consequence: A database error mid-iteration gives clients a partial user list with a 200 status. Clients cannot tell the list is incomplete.
text.fix: Check rows.Err after the loop and return a 500 error when it is not nil.

text.title: Successful response after iteration failure
text.problem: Search ignores database errors that stop row iteration.
text.consequence: Clients receive incomplete results with HTTP 200 when database iteration fails.
text.fix: Check rows.Err() before encoding results and return HTTP 500 when it reports an error.

text.title: Ignored row iteration errors
text.problem: Search ignores database errors that stop row iteration.
text.consequence: Clients receive HTTP 200 with incomplete results when database iteration fails.
text.fix: Check rows.Err() before encoding results and return HTTP 500 when it reports an error.

text.title: Row iteration error ignored in Search
text.problem: Search encodes the user list without checking rows.Err after rows.Next returns false.
text.consequence: A client receives a truncated user list with status 200 when iteration fails midway. The client cannot tell the list is incomplete.
text.fix: Check rows.Err after the loop and answer with status 500 when it returns an error.

text.title: Missing key permanently locks counter
text.problem: Count returns for an empty key without releasing the mutex.
text.consequence: Every subsequent counter request blocks indefinitely after one request omits the key.
text.fix: Validate the key before acquiring the mutex.

truth.text: Count takes the lock and returns early for a missing key without unlocking, so the next request to Count waits forever. The fix is defer h.mu.Unlock() right after Lock, or checking the key before taking the lock.

text.title: Mutex left locked on missing key
text.problem: Count returns early on an empty key while it still holds h.mu.
text.consequence: One request to GET /count without a key makes every later Count request block forever. Any caller can trigger this hang with one request.
text.fix: Validate the key before taking the lock, or unlock h.mu before the early return.

truth.text: Count takes the lock and returns early for a missing key without unlocking, so the next request to Count waits forever. The fix is defer h.mu.Unlock() right after Lock, or checking the key before taking the lock.

text.title: Unbounded growth of the hits map
text.problem: Count stores one map entry for every distinct key a client sends. The handler never evicts or limits these entries.
text.consequence: A client that sends many random keys makes the server's memory grow without bound. The process can eventually run out of memory.
text.fix: Cap the number of keys in hits, or reject unknown keys. Alternatively, use an expiring cache for the counts.

text.title: Unbounded counter storage
text.problem: Count stores arbitrary request keys without a capacity limit or eviction.
text.consequence: Callers can exhaust process memory by repeatedly submitting distinct keys.
text.fix: Enforce a storage capacity and define expiry or rejection behavior for new keys.

text.title: Unbounded growth of the hits map
text.problem: Count stores every distinct key from the query string in h.hits. The handler never removes or caps entries.
text.consequence: A client sending many unique keys grows server memory without limit. The process can eventually run out of memory.
text.fix: Cap the number of tracked keys or evict old entries. Alternatively accept only keys from a known set.

text.title: Unbounded counter storage
text.problem: Count permanently retains every distinct nonempty key supplied by callers.
text.consequence: Callers can exhaust process memory by repeatedly submitting distinct keys.
text.fix: Set a key capacity and reject new keys when the map reaches that capacity.

text.title: Concurrent saves race on one snapshot file
text.problem: Each call to onSave starts its own writeFile on SNAPSHOT while earlier writes may still run. Node does not order or serialize overlapping writeFile calls on the same file.
text.consequence: An older snapshot can finish last and overwrite a newer one. Overlapping writes can also leave mixed or truncated JSON in data/notes.json.
text.fix: Chain every snapshot write on one module-level promise so that writes run in order. Alternatively, write to a temporary file and rename it into place.

truth.text: onSave now returns a Promise, but dispatch in router.js returns the handler's result as it is and main.js passes it to res.end, which throws for a value that is not a string or a buffer; a failed write is never handled. The fix is to make dispatch async and await the handler in main.js, with an error answer when the write fails.

text.title: Snapshot keeps deleted notes
text.problem: Only onSave writes the store to data/notes.json. onDelete removes a note from the store but leaves the snapshot file unchanged.
text.consequence: The snapshot file lists deleted notes until the next save. Any reader of data/notes.json sees notes that were already deleted.
text.fix: Move the snapshot write into a shared helper. Call that helper from both onSave and onDelete after they update the store.

truth.text: onSave now returns a Promise, but dispatch in router.js returns the handler's result as it is and main.js passes it to res.end, which throws for a value that is not a string or a buffer; a failed write is never handled. The fix is to make dispatch async and await the handler in main.js, with an error answer when the write fails.

text.title: Cluster DNS lost under hostNetwork
text.problem: The pod spec adds hostNetwork true but keeps the default dnsPolicy. Kubernetes then falls back to the node resolver for this pod.
text.consequence: The worker cannot resolve in-cluster Service names. Any call from the worker to another cluster Service fails.
text.fix: Set dnsPolicy to ClusterFirstWithHostNet next to hostNetwork.

@@ -16,6 +16,8 @@ spec:
         app: image-worker
     spec:
       automountServiceAccountToken: false
+      # The worker reaches the node's image cache on localhost.
+      hostNetwork: true
       securityContext:
         runAsNonRoot: true
         runAsUser: 10001

truth.text: hostNetwork: true puts the pod in the node's network namespace: it can bind the node's ports, reach every service that listens only on the node's localhost, and is not held by network policies. The fix is to reach the image cache through a Service or a node-local address instead.

text.title: Node network exposure

text.consequence: A compromised worker can reach node services that rely on loopback isolation.
text.fix: Expose the cache through a restricted endpoint and remove hostNetwork.

text.title: Conversion containers escape pod limits and hardening
text.problem: The node's Docker daemon starts each conversion container outside the pod's cgroup. The pod's memory limit, read-only root filesystem and dropped capabilities do not apply to it.
text.consequence: A large or hostile image can use unbounded node memory and CPU without the scheduler seeing it. Kubernetes neither tracks nor cleans up those containers when the pod dies.
text.fix: Run conversions inside the worker container or as Kubernetes Jobs with their own limits and securityContext.

truth.text: Mounting the node's Docker socket gives the worker full control of the node's Docker daemon: it can start a privileged container with the node's filesystem and so become root on the node, and reach every pod there. The fix is to run each conversion without Docker access, for example as a Kubernetes Job or with a rootless builder inside the pod.

text.fix: Run conversions inside the worker container or as Kubernetes Jobs with their own resource requests and limits.

text.title: Node Docker socket mounted into the worker
text.problem: The worker pod mounts the host Docker socket at /var/run/docker.sock. The Docker daemon runs as root on the node.

text.problem: The heading puts the q URL parameter into dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping. The query text therefore reaches the DOM as live HTML.
text.consequence: An attacker can send a link such as /search?q= to run script in the victim's session. This is reflected XSS.
text.fix: Render the query as a normal JSX text child so that React escapes it.

text.title: Repeated search requests
text.problem: The effect runs after every render and updates results after every successful request.
text.consequence: Each successful response starts another request, continuously consuming browser and API resources.

text.title: Spawn failure reported as git exit code 1
text.problem: When git cannot be spawned, execFile rejects with a string code such as ENOENT and empty output. safeGit turns that string into code 1 and keeps no error message.
text.consequence: Callers cannot tell a missing git binary or missing cwd from an ordinary git failure. Users then see a misleading error with an empty stderr.
text.fix: Rethrow the error when its code is not a number. Spawn failures then stay exceptions, and only git exit codes become results.

evidence.text: return { code: typeof e.code === "number" ? e.code : 1, stdout: e.stdout ?? "", stderr: e.stderr ?? "" };

truth.text: safeGit now returns an object and no longer throws, but its callers in packages/cli still treat the result as a string (out.split, name.trim) and rely on the throw to detect a failure, so both break at run time. The fix is to update changedFiles and currentBranch to read stdout and check code, or keep the old function beside the new one.

text.title: Misleading justification for pull_request_target
text.problem: The comment says Dependabot pull requests get no secrets on pull_request. GitHub actually passes Dependabot secrets to those runs.
text.consequence: Maintainers keep the riskier pull_request_target trigger because they trust the comment. The safer pull_request trigger would work if PERCY_TOKEN were a Dependabot secret.
text.fix: Add PERCY_TOKEN as a Dependabot secret and switch the trigger to pull_request. Then rewrite the comment to match.

text.title: Privileged trigger runs pull request code with secrets
text.problem: The pull_request_target trigger runs in the base repository context with secrets. The job then checks out and runs the pull request head code.
